parsed.rationale_overall: System A provides more precise numeric grounding tied to the actual portfolio (e.g., correct 401(k) catch-up figures, specific dollar amounts from stated allocations) and better-calibrated risk levels matching the moderate profile, while System B contains some questionable claims (e.g., 9% required annualized growth, aggressive Roth conversion assumptions, 24% bracket at $220K single/joint ambiguity) and labels its dividend and rebalance recommendations with moderate risk that slightly overreach. System B is stronger on diversification (directly addressing the 22% healthcare concentration), but overall A is more actionable, better grounded, and safer.
